labels.label: bbsrem:p_p

hypotheses.note: GX.GammaLinkCircle at any p ∈ HS²; 𝔢(L) = GX.BiSusp L for every developing data Δ (OQ-126 (c)).

hypotheses.paper: « two singular points p̄, −p̄ corresponding to p and −p » (l.935–936)
hypotheses.note: the apices of GX.BiSusp L; the singularity at −p̄ is the apex of 𝔢(L⁻), L⁻ = GX.GammaLinkCircle.antipode L (Γ_{−p} = Γ_p, GX.gammaP_neg), through the flip [σ,t] ↦ [σ,π−t], an HS-isomorphism for every Δ (isIso_flip). « Singular » is not claimed: both apices are regular for L = ℓ(p) (HSSuspension's finding).

OQ-120 (a), moved p: the links are isomorphic through a B ∈ SO₀(1,2) with B • p = −p (GX.GammaLinkCircle.IsIsoVia, read through GX.linkMove); that the HS-singularity is determined by its link (l.850–852) is argued, not formalized.

hypotheses.paper: « when p is space-like … always isomorphic » (l.936–937)
hypotheses.note: proved exactly: for every move B, isomorphic through B iff L is not Misner (isIsoVia_antipode_iff, needs an oriented lifted developing pair, which every circle has); false for Misner links, which exist at every p ∈ dS² (exists_misner_not_isIsoVia_antipode).

hypotheses.paper: « p time-like: one future time-like, the other past » (l.938–939)
« future light-like singularity of degree k ≥ 1 » (l.939–940)
hypotheses.note: p ∈ ∂ℍ²₊ with an oriented lifted holonomy δᵏ g, g with a fixed point: k ≥ 1 is not used (every k); the degree at −p̄ is the same and well defined (antipode_degree, degree_unique); « vice versa » is the ∂ℍ²₋ → ∂ℍ²₊ half.
the degree-0 cases of HSSingularities' bdPlus_degree_zero / bdMinus_degree_zero; the extreme BTZ-like image is i^± minus its two tangent directions (OQ-116 (b)); antipode_cuspidal.

findings: l.936–937 « Observe that when p is space-like, p̄ and −p̄, as HS-singularities, are always isomorphic » is false as printed for Misner singularities (l.876–878), in the moved-p reading of « isomorphic » (OQ-120 (a)): the chirality vol3(p, π_p σ, e_t) of the developed space-like arc has a constant sign, ℓ(p) ≅ ℓ(−p) reverses it (GX.chirality_linkNeg), and every move B ∈ SO₀(1,2) with B p = −p, followed by Γ_{−p}, keeps it (GX.chirality_smul_linkMove_pos_iff). So the link of −p̄ is isomorphic to the link of p̄ through no move (GX.GammaLinkCircle.IsLiftedDev.not_isIsoVia_antipode); Misner links exist at every p ∈ dS² (GX.exists_misner, GX.exists_misner_not_isIsoVia_antipode). Both apices of a Misner 𝔢(L) are Misner, of opposite chiralities. The non-isomorphism of the HS-singularities themselves (not only of their links) is argued: an HS-isomorphism of punctured neighbourhoods develops to a move.

Strongest true form of l.936–937, proved: at p ∈ dS², for every move B with B • p = −p, the links of p̄ and −p̄ are isomorphic through B iff L is not a Misner link (GX.GammaLinkCircle.IsLiftedDev.isIsoVia_antipode_iff; the non-Misner half GX.GammaLinkCircle.IsLiftedDev.exists_isIsoVia_antipode covers BTZ-like past/future and every degree k ≠ 0). Suggested wording: « when p is space-like and L is not a Misner circle, p̄ and −p̄ are isomorphic; when L is a Misner circle they are both Misner, of opposite chiralities, and not isomorphic ».

Outside the label, l.850–852 (« the ℝP¹-structure and the additional data of i^±(L) determine the (Γ_p, ℓ(p))-structure on the link, hence the HS-singular point »): argued false for Misner links, from the same chirality lemmas. At a fixed p ∈ dS², let g be the lift with fixed points of some ρ ∈ Γ_p ∖ {1}. The two space-like components of {g ≠ id} in one turn of ℝP̃¹ are translates of each other by 1, so g − id has one sign on both, and they project to the two antipodal space-like arcs of ℓ(p), of opposite chiralities. Their quotients are two Misner circles with the same lifted holonomy (g or g⁻¹), hence isomorphic ℝP¹-circles (GX.rp1Iso_iff_conj), both with i^±(L) = ∅. They are not (Γ_p, ℓ(p))-isomorphic, since Γ_p keeps the chirality. So for each holonomy the Misner type of l.876–878 splits in two (left and right). This is not formalized as a same-p statement; the formal content is the move version above.
Precision (l.935–936, already HSSuspension's finding): the « two singular points » are regular for the regular link L = ℓ(p).
questions: OQ-120 (a), evidence requested: « isomorphic » for HS-singularities at p and −p cannot be read with the same p (p ≠ −p); the remark needs isomorphisms through a move. Reading taken: GX.GammaLinkCircle.IsIsoVia (a homeomorphism reading in the charts as B ∈ SO₀(1,2), B • p = −p, followed by an element of Γ_{−p}). Under it the space-like sentence holds exactly for non-Misner links and for every move (not only the half-turn); moves keep i^±, the orientation, and the chirality of space-like directions. The planner's [r] claim in the target's evidence (« it can be proved with the half-turn … needs no ruling ») is refuted for Misner links.

« as HS-singularities » (l.937): read through the links; that the HS-singularity is determined by its link (l.850–852) and conversely that an HS-isomorphism of the singularities induces a moved-p isomorphism of the links are argued, not formalized. Should either direction be a target (it would turn the link statements into statements about HS-singularities)?

OQ-126 (c), (d): 𝔢(L) built from developing data Δ (GX.BiSusp with GX.GammaLinkCircle.DevData.suspStructure); the flip 𝔢(L) ≅ 𝔢(L⁻) is proved for every Δ, Δ-independence is not formalized. OQ-104 rides along through SingularHSStructure.IsIso.

OQ-113 (c): orientations HS² outward normal first, θ oriented; at −p the oriented identification is GX.tangentNeg θ (T_p = T_{−p} reverses the orientation, complex conjugation restores it); the degree at −p̄ is read through it.
OQ-116 (a) (time-like i^± at dS²: the BTZ-like/Misner split of the space-like sentence uses it) and OQ-116 (b) (the past extreme BTZ-like image is i⁺(ℓ(−p)) minus its two tangent directions).
OQ-120 (c) / OQ-124: positive and negative read in the l.915 form (IsSpacelikePositive), for the side result that signs are kept across the apices (not stated in the paper).
« degree k ≥ 1 » (l.939–940): read as an oriented lifted holonomy δᵏ g with g having a fixed point; the hypothesis k ≥ 1 is not used (the degree is kept for every k).

kb_proposals: At p ∈ dS² every N ∈ SO₀(1,2) with N p = −p is an involution (GX.mul_self_eq_one_of_apply_neg): on T_pHS², [N] = GX.tpReflect reverses linkArea and keeps Q∘π_p; write [N]n₁, [N]n₂ in the light-like basis by Cramer (eq_add_of_linkArea_ne_zero), a·c = 0 from nullity (GX.minkB_comb_of_null), and the area/form identities (GX.linkArea_comb) make it antidiagonal with product 1. Hence B ρ B⁻¹ = ρ⁻¹ for ρ ∈ Γ_p (GX.conj_eq_inv_of_neg: B and Bρ are both involutions).

To lift an orientation-reversing map of ℓ(p), e.g. GX.linkReflect B = ℓ(−p)⁻¹ ∘ B, to ℝP̃¹: θ_B = tangentNeg θ ∘ [B] (GX.tangentMove) is oriented, linkMove B ∘ linkCover θ_B = linkCover (tangentNeg θ) (GX.linkMove_linkCover), and exists_rayLift with A = 1 between θ and θ_B gives F ∈ G̃ with R̂(linkCover θ t) = linkCover θ (−F t) (GX.exists_linkReflect_linkCover).

Two lifts through linkCover of the same map differ by a constant 2n (linkCover_lift_eq); pin n at a light-like lift: the lifted holonomy f moves every light-like lift by the same 2m (δ^{−2m} f fixes one, hence all by fixed_iff_null, or is 1 when ρ = 1).

A (moved) isomorphism of (Γ_p, ℓ(p))-circles from a lifted developing pair: Φ = D⁻¹ ∘ K ∘ D by `choose` on K (D s) ∈ range D; an antitone Φ is continuous via Monotone.continuous_of_surjective on −Φ; descend through the periodic cover as in GX.exists_rp1Iso_of_conj (Classical.choose of hE.surjective, hE.fiber, IsQuotientMap.continuous_iff); the chart condition from hd s and hd (Φ s), pushed to L by isOpenMap.image_mem_nhds (GX.GammaLinkCircle.IsLiftedDev.exists_isIsoVia_antipode).

Two open intervals of ℝ whose ends satisfy P, with no P-point inside, and which meet, are equal (GX.Ioo_eq_of_ends): with P = « light-like lift » it identifies a developed degree-0 interval with its image up to δ^{2j}.

Pitfall: with A : GammaP C.antipode.pt expected, `gammaNeg C.pt X • linkMove B hB σ` fails instance search (HSMul (GammaP (−C.pt)) (Link C.antipode.pt)); bind `let A : GammaP C.antipode.pt := gammaNeg C.pt X` and close the rewrite chain with rfl.
Pitfall: `rw [← h2]` with h2 : f (y − 2m) = y rewrites every y in the goal, the right-hand side included; use `conv_lhs => rw [← h2]`.
